question: If 50 is subtracted from 60% of a number, then the result is 40. 60% of the same number is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the question, **60% of a number − 50 = 40**.

Directly solving for the required value: **60% of the number = 40 + 50**.

**⇒ 60% of the number = 90**.

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/03e8d74b21eece0c30bbfc6aba57bd4a0db212e33a913211b375542dd719c0ec.png] 

Let the **number** be **x**.

Given: **60% of x − 50 = 40**

⇒ **(60/100) × x − 50 = 40**

⇒ **0.6x − 50 = 40**

⇒ **0.6x = 40 + 50**

⇒ **0.6x = 90**

The question asks for **60% of the same number**, which is **0.6x**.

⇒ **Required Value = 90**

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert **60%** to a fraction: **60/100 = 3/5**. The equation becomes **(3/5)x − 50 = 40**.

Finding the Original Number

If the question asked for the **original number**: **0.6x = 90** → **x = 90 ÷ 0.6 = 150**.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of **a%** and **b%**, the net percentage change is **[a + b + (ab/100)]%**.</p
